TLS certificate about to expire

A certificate needs renewing before browsers and clients start rejecting it. All playbooks.

  1. Check the dates on the certificate the server is actually serving.

    Check a remote TLS certificate's expiry

    Fetches and displays the expiration date of a remote SSL certificate.

    echo | openssl s_client -servername example.com -connect example.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates

    ssl, tls, certificate

  2. Create a new key and certificate signing request for your CA.

    Generate CSR and private key

    Creates a new 2048-bit RSA private key and a Certificate Signing Request.

    openssl req -new -newkey rsa:2048 -nodes -keyout mydomain.key -out mydomain.csr

    The private key is written unencrypted (-nodes); keep mydomain.key private.

    ssl, openssl, csr

  3. Check the new certificate's subject, alternative names and dates.

    Read a local certificate file

    Reads an x509 certificate file and outputs its details.

    openssl x509 -in certificate.crt -text -noout

    ssl, openssl, verify

  4. After installing it, test the Nginx configuration.

    Test Nginx configuration

    Tests the Nginx config files for syntax errors before reloading.

    sudo nginx -t

    nginx, config, test

  5. Reload Nginx without dropping connections, then check the served dates again.

    Reload Nginx gracefully

    Reloads the Nginx configuration without dropping active connections.

    sudo nginx -s reload

    nginx, reload
